title: Ruby or Rails stack frame disclosed in a response
description: The response body contains a Ruby backtrace line of the form path/file.rb:LINE:in. A framework that renders an unhandled exception in production hands an attacker the file layout, method names and library versions of the application. The check reports the disclosed frame; it does not claim the exception itself is exploitable.
remediation: Disable detailed exception rendering in production (config.consider_all_requests_local = false for Rails, or an equivalent handler) and return a generic error page with a correlation id.
limitation: Observation-level: matches one Ruby backtrace frame in the captured body. A custom error page that echoes a single file path without the :in marker is not reported.
scopeT: One response body: confirm a Ruby stack frame line.
fp: A documentation page that shows an example backtrace, or a debug route enabled only for operators, is reported by design; the limitation states this.
recordDesc: A response discloses a Ruby stack frame. Production error pages should never carry interpreter backtraces: the file path maps the source tree, the method name maps internal call structure, and the gem paths disclose exact dependency versions that can be matched against known issues.
applicability: Ruby and Rails applications that render unhandled exceptions.
risk: Source layout and dependency versions disclosed to any requester; MEDIUM severity.
why: The body contains a Ruby backtrace frame with a source path and line number.
fix: Render a generic error page in production.
verifyT: Request the failing route and confirm the response contains no .rb:LINE:in frame.

cells.safe: We could not complete that request.

title: Python http.server directory listing exposed
description: The response body is the directory index generated by Python's http.server or SimpleHTTPServer module. Serving a directory instead of a fixed document exposes every file beneath it, including backups and configuration left in the tree. The check reports the generated listing page, not the presence of specific files.
remediation: Serve an explicit application or static index, disable directory browsing, and remove non-public files from the served tree.
limitation: Observation-level: matches the generic listing title emitted by the Python standard-library servers. Directory listings from other servers are covered by separate rules.
scopeT: One response body: confirm the Python directory-listing title.
fp: A deliberately public file mirror is reported by design; the limitation states this.
recordDesc: A Python standard-library server renders a directory index. The listing exposes file names, sizes and timestamps for the whole directory, and directories served this way often contain source archives and editor backups that were never meant to be fetched.
applicability: Python http.server or SimpleHTTPServer deployments reachable from untrusted networks.
risk: Directory contents enumerable by any requester; MEDIUM severity.
why: The response is the auto-generated Python directory listing page.
fix: Remove non-public files from the served directory.
verifyT: Request the directory URL and confirm the response is an application page, not a generated index.

title: CORS allows every HTTP method from any origin
description: The Access-Control-Allow-Methods response header declares a wildcard, so a browser preflight accepts any method the resource implements from any origin. Combined with a permissive origin policy this widens the set of cross-origin calls a page can make. The check reads the declared method list; it does not claim that a state-changing method is actually reachable.
remediation: List the methods the API actually serves (for example GET, POST, OPTIONS) and keep the origin allowlist explicit.
limitation: Observation-level: evaluates the Access-Control-Allow-Methods header alone. Whether a dangerous method is implemented, and whether credentials are allowed, requires separate evidence.
scopeT: One response: confirm a wildcard method declaration.
fp: A public, unauthenticated read-only API may accept every method by design; it is still reported because the header cannot express that distinction.
recordDesc: A CORS policy grants every HTTP method to every origin. Method wildcards are frequently added to stop preflight failures during development and then shipped unchanged; they turn a narrowly scoped API into one that accepts cross-origin PUT or DELETE if those routes exist.
applicability: HTTP APIs that answer CORS preflight requests.
risk: Cross-origin method surface widened for any origin; LOW severity.
why: The method response header contains a wildcard entry.
verifyT: Send a preflight and confirm Access-Control-Allow-Methods lists only documented methods.

title: Werkzeug interactive debugger page disclosed
description: The response body is the Werkzeug interactive debugger page, which a Flask application renders when debug mode is enabled. The page exposes a traceback with source context and offers an interactive console; the console is gated by a PIN, so the check reports the exposed debugger rather than remote code execution.
remediation: Run production deployments with debug disabled (app.run(debug=False) or the WSGI server default) and return a generic error page.
limitation: Observation-level: matches the debugger's identifying page text. It does not determine whether the console PIN is guessable or whether code execution is possible.
scopeT: One response body: confirm the Werkzeug debugger page.
fp: A deliberately exposed debugger on an isolated development host is reported by design; the limitation states this.
recordDesc: A response carries the Werkzeug debugger console page. Debug mode is the most common Flask production mistake: the interactive console exposes the stack, local variables and environment of the failing request, and the PIN that guards it has been bypassed in public research for years.
applicability: Flask and Werkzeug deployments reachable from untrusted networks.
risk: Source, locals and an interactive console disclosed to requesters; MEDIUM severity.
why: The response is the Werkzeug interactive debugger page.
fix: Render a generic error page and log server-side.
verifyT: Trigger an error and confirm the response is a generic page with no debugger console.

title: Form submits to a plaintext HTTP action on an HTTPS page
description: An HTTPS page contains a form whose action is an absolute http:// URL. Submitting it sends every field, including credentials or payment details, over plaintext even though the page itself was delivered securely. The check reports the downgrade target; it does not claim the destination is attacker-controlled.
remediation: Point the form action at an https:// URL, or use a relative action so the browser keeps the page's scheme.
limitation: Observation-level: only observations fetched over HTTPS are judged. Subresource downloads are covered by the separate mixed-content rule.
scopeT: One HTTPS response body: confirm a form action with a plaintext scheme.
fp: A form posted to a plaintext endpoint that carries no sensitive fields is reported by design; the header-level check cannot classify field content.
recordDesc: A secure page posts a form to a plaintext endpoint. Browsers no longer block form submission as active mixed content, so the request leaves the browser over HTTP and is readable and modifiable by any network observer. The failure usually appears when a checkout or login endpoint is configured per environment and the scheme is left behind.
risk: Form fields readable and modifiable in transit; MEDIUM severity.
why: The form's action URL uses the http scheme on an HTTPS page.
fix: Prefer a relative action so the page scheme is inherited.
verifyT: Inspect the rendered page and confirm every form action resolves to https.

title: .NET stack frame with source path disclosed in a response
description: The response body contains a .NET stack frame in the form 'in <path>.cs:line N'. The captured frame discloses the assembly names, method signatures and build path of the application. The check reports the disclosed frame; it does not claim the caller can reach the failing code path deliberately.
remediation: Disable developer exception pages in production and return a generic error response with a correlation id.
limitation: Observation-level: requires the source path and :line marker that the developer exception page emits. Frames without a source file are out of scope.
scopeT: One response body: confirm a .NET frame with a source path.
fp: A deliberately verbose internal endpoint is reported by design; the limitation states this.
recordDesc: A response discloses a .NET stack frame with a source path. The developer exception page is convenient during development and catastrophic in production: it names internal types, exposes the build directory and often includes configuration values in the surrounding output.
applicability: ASP.NET and ASP.NET Core applications that render developer exception pages.
risk: Internal type names and build paths disclosed; MEDIUM severity.
why: The body contains a .NET frame carrying a source path and line number.
fix: Disable the developer exception page in production.
verifyT: Trigger an exception and confirm the response carries no .cs:line frame.
